source.title: Hydrogel Matrix to Support Stem Cell Survival After Brain Transplantation in Stroke

material: Hyaluronan–heparin–collagen hydrogel (HyStem-HP) with ES cell-derived NPCs

formulation.evidence: 100 000 NPCs in 1 mL saline were mixed with 4 mL hyaluronan/heparin, 1 mL gelatin, and 1 mL cross-linker.
100 000 NPCs in 1 mL saline were mixed with 4 mL hyaluronan/heparin, 1 mL gelatin, and 1 mL cross-linker.
100 000 NPCs in 1 mL saline were mixed with 4 mL hyaluronan/heparin, 1 mL gelatin, and 1 mL cross-linker.

processing.evidence: into the infarct cavity at a depth of 1 mm from the surface of the brain at a rate of 0.7 mL/min.

biology.cell_type: GFP mouse embryonic stem cell-derived neural progenitor cells (ES-NPCs)

other_outcomes.evidence: there is also a significant decrease of Iba1-positive cell infiltration into the graft with the hydrogel (31 ± 7/mm³ without hydrogel vs 19 ± 4/mm³ with hydrogel; P = .003
other_outcomes.name: Iba1-positive cell infiltration into graft

survival.evidence: An average of 300 cells in the cells-only group survived, and an average of 600 cells in the hydrogel group survived, which is a statistically significant 2-fold expansion in cell survival (P = .002)

notes: Transplanted into stroke cavity 7 days after photothrombotic stroke. Main text states '0.3% and 0.6% of transplanted cells survive with or without hydrogel, respectively', which conflicts with figure caption (600 cells with hydrogel). ES-NPCs remained undifferentiated. In vitro hydrogel increased survival (LDH, tetrazolium) in culture; values only in figures.
